headline: Senior Backend Engineer (Node.js / TypeScript)
summary: Backend engineer with {years}+ years building and running production services, currently on industrial IoT at Company A: factory-monitoring and device-control backends that ingest machine data from factory gateways, write values back to machines on the shop floor, and deploy to on-premise and edge hardware. Since 2023 at Company B I have been the main backend author of Node.js/TypeScript marketplace and payments platforms, where a dropped or duplicated transaction has a direct cost. I specialise in event-driven and real-time services that talk to systems whose timing cannot be trusted (devices, ERPs, blockchain networks, payment providers) and stay correct under retries, delays and partial failure.

paragraphs: I’m applying for the Backend Software Engineer role. What stands out to me is that the backend here sits between software and physical devices in a POS environment: when a terminal drops its connection or a command arrives twice, a sale is lost or a payment is wrong. That is close to what I do today at Company A, and to the payment systems I built before that.

At Company A I build backends for industrial monitoring in manufacturing plants. Machine data comes in from factory gateways and becomes production events and KPIs. I also built the path in the other direction: when a work order starts, the backend writes product, mould and cycle-time values back to the machine’s gateway, with per-machine tag mapping, an enable toggle that needs explicit confirmation, a local kill switch and locking against concurrent writes. A wrong value on a running machine is worse than no value, so the safeguards came first. I hardened the device endpoints’ authentication, built the SAP confirmation pipeline with an outbox and retries, and automated deployments to on-premise factory VMs.

Since 2023 I have also worked with Company B, part-time since this year, on Node.js/TypeScript marketplace platforms: I am the main backend author of its core API (PostgreSQL, Redis, BullMQ), built marketplace services on MongoDB with real-time chat over Socket.IO, and built the USDC deposit and escrow flows on Avalanche. Earlier, at Company E, I built fiat-to-crypto payment flows and a scheduled job that reconciles transactions against the chain.

My device work so far has been over network protocols such as HTTP and WebSockets. The hard parts carry over to any transport: devices that answer late or not at all, connections that need supervising, and commands that must be safe to retry. I have also written C++ and Rust, and I expect to be productive at the native layer quickly.
I’m open to relocating to Amsterdam, and I would welcome the chance to discuss how I can help make your device-facing services robust.
